luke.14.p1.b1.text: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat in the home of a leading Pharisee, and those in attendance were watching Him closely.

luke.14.p1.b2.text: Right there before Him was a man with dropsy.

luke.14.p2.b1.text: “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?”

luke.14.p2.b2.text: But they remained silent. Then Jesus took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him on his way.

luke.14.p2.b3.text: “Which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day will not immediately pull him out?”

luke.14.p2.b4.text: And they were unable to answer these questions.

luke.14.p3.b1.text: When Jesus noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, He told them a parable:

luke.14.p3.b2.text: “When you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not sit in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited.

luke.14.p4.b1.text: But when you are invited, go and sit in the last place,

luke.14.p4.b2.text: ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’

luke.14.p4.b3.text: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

luke.14.p5.b1.text: Then Jesus said to the man who had invited Him, “When you host a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or brothers or relatives or rich neighbors.

luke.14.p5.b2.text: But when you host a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind,

luke.14.p5.b3.text: and you will be blessed. Since they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”

luke.14.p6.b1.text: “Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.”

luke.14.p6.b2.text: But Jesus replied, “A certain man prepared a great banquet and invited many guests.

luke.14.p7.b1.text: But one after another they all began to make excuses.

luke.14.p7.b2.text: ‘I have bought a field, and I need to go see it. Please excuse me.’

luke.14.p7.b3.text: ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.’

luke.14.p7.b4.text: ‘I have married a wife, so I cannot come.’

luke.14.p8.b1.text: The servant returned and reported all this to his master.

luke.14.p8.b2.text: ‘Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city, and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.’

luke.14.p8.b3.text: ‘Sir,’ … ‘what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.’

luke.14.p9.b1.text: ‘Go out to the highways and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house will be full.

luke.14.p9.b2.text: For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my banquet.’”

luke.14.p10.b1.text: Large crowds were now traveling with Jesus, and He turned and said to them,

luke.14.p10.b2.text: “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters—

luke.14.p10.b3.text: yes, even his own life—he cannot be My disciple.

luke.14.p10.b4.text: And whoever does not carry his cross and follow Me cannot be My disciple.

luke.14.p11.b1.text: Which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost to see if he has the resources to complete it?

luke.14.p11.b2.text: Otherwise, if he lays the foundation and is unable to finish the work,

luke.14.p11.b3.text: everyone who sees it will ridicule him,

luke.14.p11.b4.text: saying, ‘This man could not finish what he started to build.’

luke.14.p12.b1.text: Or what king on his way to war with another king will not first sit down and consider whether he can engage with ten thousand men the one coming against him with twenty thousand?

luke.14.p12.b2.text: And if he is unable, he will send a delegation while the other king is still far off, to ask for terms of peace.

luke.14.p12.b3.text: In the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple.

luke.14.p12.b4.text: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its savor, with what will it be seasoned? … it is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
